The region enclosed by the curves $y=x$ and $y=\sqrt{x}$ for $y\in [0,1]$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=3.$ Find the volume of the resulting solid.

current_example.problem:
The region enclosed by the curves $x=y^2$ and $x=2-y^2$ is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the line $x=-1.$ Find the volume of the resulting solid.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/e8f0f999521058f3213e11bd3df67a95a6ea8604e6853d06923ffbba6cf9d17c.png)
current_example.worked_solution:
First, to determine the limits of integration, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =2-{y}^{2} \\ 2{y}^{2} & =2 \\ {y}^{2} & =1 \\ y & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, our limits of integration are from $y=-1$ to $y=1.$

Next, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/c3c9217600a26e11614752b2ca2ac8b3aa6c12b0df9f3a8c13d2b32c5b338107.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x=y^2,$ and

- *leaves* though the outer curve $x={2-y^2}.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of outer and inner solids.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x={2-y^2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/3696bac064f5157b5c4ab3aefe34128d2d126a0a6b586106eb1e439bc90e7df5.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}{[\,(2-{y}^{2})-(-1)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}{[3-{y}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=y^2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/f59ee5966f0cb9572d00e7f7278a7462841aef6b18f4865924303ad65b50738c.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}[\,({y}^{2})-(-1)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}{[{y}^{2}+1]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}{[3-{y}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x-\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}{[{y}^{2}+1]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}({[3-{y}^{2}]}^{2}-{[{y}^{2}+1]}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}(8-8{y}^{2})\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {(8y-\frac{8{y}^{3}}{3})|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\pi [(8-\frac{8}{3})-(-8+\frac{8}{3})] \\  & =\pi (\frac{32}{3}) \\  & =\frac{32\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
